hook: The man with sport's longest winning streak has a sad story behind it.
story: The sport is squash: two players sealed in a walled court, hitting the same ball off the front wall until one of them breaks. Jahangir Khan of Pakistan was world champion at seventeen, the youngest ever. Then, from 1981 to 1986, he simply did not lose: 555 consecutive matches, the longest winning streak in professional sport, per Guinness. He once won a professional final without conceding a single point.
number: When Ross Norman finally beat him, at the 1986 World Open final, five years had passed between defeats.
closer: And the sad story? In 1979, his older brother Torsam, also a professional, collapsed and died in the middle of a match. Jahangir was fifteen. He nearly quit. Instead, all 555 were for his brother.
full_text: The man with sport's longest winning streak has a sad story behind it. The sport is squash: two players sealed in a walled court, hitting the same ball off the front wall until one of them breaks. Jahangir Khan of Pakistan was world champion at seventeen, the youngest ever. Then, from 1981 to 1986, he simply did not lose: 555 consecutive matches, the longest winning streak in professional sport, per Guinness. He once won a professional final without conceding a single point. When Ross Norman finally beat him, at the 1986 World Open final, five years had passed between defeats. And the sad story? In 1979, his older brother Torsam, also a professional, collapsed and died in the middle of a match. Jahangir was fifteen. He nearly quit. Instead, all 555 were for his brother.
